paper.title: SO+ FLUORESCENCE FROM PENNING IONIZATION OF SO2
paper.affiliation: Research Institute of Industrial Science, Kyushu University, Hakozaki, Fukuoka 812 (Japan)
paper.journal: International Journal of Mass Spectrometry and Ion Physics

research.topic: Penning ionization of SO2 by He(2^3S) metastable atoms and fluorescence spectroscopy of resulting ionic and neutral species
research.method: Flowing afterglow apparatus with microwave discharge (2450 MHz, 80 W) to generate He(2^3S); emission spectroscopy (200-510 nm) using scanning monochromator (1200 lines/mm grating) and photomultiplier detection
key_findings: Identification of SO2+ C^2B_2(v1',0,0) → X^2A_1(v1'',0,0) fluorescence system (origin at 3376 ± 2 Å)
Determination of symmetric stretching vibrational frequencies: X^2A_1 = 1259 ± 13 cm^{-1}, C^2B_2 = 788 ± 14 cm^{-1}
Major reaction channel is Penning ionization into C^2B_2 state of SO2+; molecular excitation (SO2*) and dissociative excitation (SO*) are minor
SO(A^3Π → X^3Σ^-) and SO2(A^1B_1 → X^1A_1) emissions also observed

X^2A_1.description: Ground ionic state (adiabatic IP = 12.305 eV), symmetric stretch frequency 1259 ± 13 cm^{-1}

C^2B_2.description: Excited ionic state (IP = 15.977 eV for v1=0), symmetric stretch frequency 788 ± 14 cm^{-1}

SO2.A^1B_1: Continuous emission assigned to A^1B_1 → X^1A_1 transition

O2+.A^2Π_u → X^2Π_g: Predominant emission in He(2^3S) + O2 reaction, used for comparison

He.2^3S: Metastable state (19.8 eV), primary energy carrier
He.2^1S: Rapidly converts to 2^3S by electron collisions

theory.analysis_method: Vibrational assignment based on high-resolution photoelectron spectroscopy data (Eland & Danby [1], Turner et al. [2], Lloyd & Roberts [3])
theory.energy_level_diagram: Constructed using excitation energies of SO2 [8] and SO [9], ionization energies of SO2 [1,3], O [10], SO [11], and dissociation energy D(OS-O) = 5.5 eV [12]
theory.transition_energy_calculation: Calculated using vibrational intervals from photoelectron data; Delandres table constructed for C^2B_2 → X^2A_1 transition
theory.assignment_criteria: Agreement between observed band origin (29620 ± 18 cm^{-1}) and photoelectron estimates (29730 ± 121 [1], 29682 ± 161 [2] cm^{-1}); consistency of vibrational progressions

features: Strong SO2+ C^2B_2 → X^2A_1 band system 310-510 nm

observables.intensity_distribution: Irregular variations in two-component SO+ (a^4Π → X^2Π) ruled out by O2 comparison

results.main_conclusion: Penning ionization of SO2 by He(2^3S) predominantly produces SO2+ in the C^2B_2 state, yielding strong fluorescence not observed with other excitation methods (VUV photons, 75-350 eV electrons, 2-3 keV Ar+ ions)

vibrational_frequencies_determined.X^2A_1: 1259 ± 13 cm^{-1} (antibonding character of sulfur lone-pair 8a1 orbital)
vibrational_frequencies_determined.C^2B_2: 788 ± 14 cm^{-1} (strongly bonding nature of 2b2 orbital in S-O)

results.ionization_potentials: Listed in Table 2 for vibrational levels of X^2A_1 and C^2B_2, agreeing with photoelectron data
results.excluded_transitions: SO+ (a^4Π → X^2Π) emission excluded by comparison with O2+ spectrum
results.previous_work_correction: Wu and Yencha [5] assigned the 16.0 eV state to B; this work assigns it to C^2B_2 based on Lloyd & Roberts [3]

figures.Fig.1: Schematic diagram of flowing afterglow apparatus (quartz flow tube 12 mm diameter, Pyrex reaction cell 35 mm diameter, microwave discharge, charged particle deflector, quartz window, monochromator)
figures.Fig.2: Typical emission spectrum of SO2 in helium afterglow (240-460 nm), showing continuous features and discrete bands; stray He I lines marked
figures.Fig.3: Energy-level diagram of possible products in He(2^3S) + SO2 reaction, using literature excitation/ionization energies and dissociation energy
figures.Fig.4: Fluorescence spectrum of SO2+ [C^2B_2(v1',0,0) → X^2A_1(v1'',0,0)] system (310-510 nm), with vibrational assignments and stray He I lines marked

equations.transition_energy: Calculated from vibrational intervals: ΔE = E(C, v1') - E(X, v1'')
equations.ionization_potential: IP(v1) = IP(0,0,0) + hc × ω_e × v1 (for harmonic approximation)

limitations.assignment_uncertainties: Discrepancy between observed band origin and photoelectron estimates in previous work (Wu & Yencha [5])
limitations.SO+_exclusion: SO+ (a^4Π → X^2Π) emission not definitively ruled out but excluded by analogy with O2+ spectrum
limitations.SO2_fluorescence: Discrete SO2 fluorescence bands not observed; only continuous emission assigned to A^1B_1 → X^1A_1
limitations.spectral_resolution: Medium resolution (8.3 Å/mm) limits fine structure analysis
limitations.pressure_effects: He pressure 1-2 torr may cause collisional quenching
